gaps.lead: Nadia's friend arrived just as she was about to leave the restaurant.
gaps.sentence: Nadia was ___ the restaurant when her friend arrived.
gaps.hint: be about to = be on the point of + -ing
gaps.explanation: 'About to leave' becomes 'on the point of leaving'.

gaps.lead: The staff wear a uniform at all times.
gaps.sentence: The staff ___ a uniform at all times.

gaps.lead: Her French improved because she spent years in Lyon.
gaps.sentence: Her French improved as ___ in Lyon.
gaps.explanation: as a result of + noun/-ing = because of.

gaps.lead: Most of the children ignored what the teacher had told them.
gaps.sentence: Few of the children ___ what the teacher had told them.

gaps.lead: The film we saw last week was better than this one.
gaps.sentence: This film is not ___ the one we saw last week.
gaps.explanation: 'Not as good as' expresses an inferior comparison.

gaps.lead: Jogging every morning was completely normal for him.
gaps.explanation: be used to + -ing = be accustomed to.
